questions.question: What shape is a speed limit sign?

options.text: School crossing sign.
Railroad crossing sign.
Stop sign.
Speed limit sign.

questions.correctAnswerText: Speed limit sign.
questions.explanation: Speed limit signs are rectangular with white background and black text. They tell you the rules of the road. You must follow them.

questions.question: Where is the gearshift lever on a motorcycle?

options.text: In front of the left footrest
In front of the right footrest
On the left handgrip
On the right handgrip

questions.correctAnswerText: In front of the left footrest
questions.explanation: The gearshift lever is in front of the left footrest. You operate it with your left foot.

questions.question: When passing parked cars, what should you prepare for?

options.text: Open parking spaces.
A car suddenly pulling out into traffic.
Parking meters.
Other drivers seeing you and staying away.

questions.correctAnswerText: A car suddenly pulling out into traffic.
questions.explanation: A parked car may suddenly pull out into traffic. Ride on the left side of your lane to give yourself more space from parked cars on the right.

questions.question: How often does a motorcycle need maintenance compared to a car?

options.text: Less often.
More often.
Only by a mechanic.
Only at a dealer.

questions.correctAnswerText: More often.
questions.explanation: Small problems on a motorcycle are more serious than on a car. Check your motorcycle before every ride.

questions.question: If you are riding next to another vehicle, what should you do?

options.text: Speed up or slow down.
Wave at the other driver.
Stay alongside until the next exit.
Let the other driver worry about it.

questions.correctAnswerText: Speed up or slow down.
questions.explanation: Riding next to another vehicle is dangerous. The vehicle may be hiding you from other drivers, and you may not be able to escape if a hazard appears. Speed up or fall back.

questions.question: Where should you ride in your lane to see better before passing?

options.text: In the left portion of your lane.
In the right portion of your lane.
In the center of your lane.
Stand up on your motorcycle.

questions.correctAnswerText: In the left portion of your lane.
questions.explanation: Ride in the left portion of your lane when preparing to pass. This helps you see ahead better and makes oncoming traffic more aware of you.

questions.question: What should you assume when riding a motorcycle?

options.text: Other drivers can see you as easily as other vehicles.
Other drivers cannot see you.
You don't need to worry about being seen.
Ride aggressively.

questions.correctAnswerText: Other drivers cannot see you.
questions.explanation: Motorcycles are small and hard to see. Ride defensively and assume other drivers do not see you.

questions.question: What protective gear is most important?

options.text: A jacket with exposed arms.
Boots with tall heels.
Leather gloves.
Shoes that stop below the ankle.

questions.correctAnswerText: Leather gloves.
questions.explanation: Wear leather gloves to protect your hands. Also wear a jacket and pants that cover your arms and legs. Wear sturdy boots that cover your ankles with low heels.

questions.question: How should you stop quickly?

options.text: Use only the rear brake.
Use only the front brake.
Use both brakes.
Use the rear brake firmly, then add front brake pressure slowly.

questions.correctAnswerText: Use both brakes.
questions.explanation: To stop quickly, use both brakes at the same time.

questions.question: What happens if you shift to a lower gear while going too fast?

options.text: The motorcycle will jerk and the rear tire may skid.
The motorcycle will speed up too quickly.
The front tire will likely skid.
The engine will make a loud noise.

questions.correctAnswerText: The motorcycle will jerk and the rear tire may skid.
questions.explanation: If you shift to a lower gear without slowing down enough, the motorcycle will jerk and the rear wheel may skid.

questions.question: When turning on a motorcycle, what should you do?

options.text: Keep your eyes focused on the front of the motorcycle.
Look ahead through the turn to where you want to go.
Turn your entire body to see through the turn.
Speed up before the turn.

questions.correctAnswerText: Look ahead through the turn to where you want to go.
questions.explanation: When turning, look through the turn toward where you want to go. Turn only your head, not your shoulders. Keep your eyes level with the horizon.

questions.question: When a group of riders enters a curve, how should they ride?

options.text: In a single-file line.
In a staggered formation.
In pairs.
On the shoulder.

questions.correctAnswerText: In a single-file line.
questions.explanation: Riders should switch to a single-file line when turning, taking curves, or entering or exiting a highway. Staggered formation is best at other times.

questions.question: What should you NOT do on a slippery surface?

options.text: Reduce your speed.
Avoid making sudden moves.
Use only the front brake when slowing or stopping.
Use both brakes when slowing or stopping.

questions.correctAnswerText: Use only the front brake when slowing or stopping.
questions.explanation: On slippery surfaces, use both brakes when slowing or stopping. Also reduce your speed and avoid sudden moves. Be careful on oily areas, dirt, gravel, shaded areas, and bridges—they are more slippery than other surfaces.

questions.question: How can you reduce your reaction time?

options.text: Ride slower than the speed limit.
Keep your fingers over the clutch and brake levers.
Shift into neutral when slowing.
Pull in the clutch when turning.

questions.correctAnswerText: Keep your fingers over the clutch and brake levers.
questions.explanation: Keep your fingers over the clutch and brake levers to reduce your reaction time. This is especially important when riding through areas where hazards might appear.

questions.question: What is the best lane position?

options.text: The one that lets you travel the fastest.
The one that allows you to draft off other vehicles.
The one that allows other drivers to see you.
The one that places you in other vehicles' blind spots.

questions.correctAnswerText: The one that allows other drivers to see you.
questions.explanation: Choose a lane position that allows you to be seen by other drivers and to see them. It should help you avoid wind blasts, blind spots, and hazards. It should discourage other drivers from sharing your lane and give you an escape route if needed. Maximize your space cushion.

questions.question: What should you consider when choosing a lane position?

options.text: Whether other drivers can see you.
How many cars are ahead on the road.
Which part of the lane will make your trip shorter.
If you can pass more vehicles in a certain position.

questions.correctAnswerText: Whether other drivers can see you.
questions.explanation: Make sure your lane position allows other drivers to see you. You should also maintain an adequate space cushion around your motorcycle.

questions.question: What should your lane position NOT do?

options.text: Increase your ability to see and be seen.
Help you avoid surface hazards.
Provide you with an escape route.
Invite other drivers into your lane.

questions.correctAnswerText: Invite other drivers into your lane.
questions.explanation: Your lane position should increase your ability to see and be seen, help you avoid hazards and wind blasts, keep you out of blind spots, and give you an escape route. Position yourself so that other drivers do not want to share your lane.

questions.question: When braking on a surface with poor traction, what should you do?

options.text: Apply the brakes faster than usual.
Apply the brakes more gently than usual.
Do not use the rear brake.
Do not use the front brake.

questions.correctAnswerText: Apply the brakes more gently than usual.
questions.explanation: On surfaces with poor traction, apply the brakes more gently than normal to avoid skidding.

questions.question: What should a rider do when entering a turn?

options.text: Speed up.
Reduce their speed.
Lean their shoulders to match the turn angle.
Sit as high as possible.

questions.correctAnswerText: Reduce their speed.
questions.explanation: Before entering a turn, reduce your speed by releasing the throttle and using the brakes if needed.

questions.question: How should you stop quickly?

options.text: Use only the front brake.
Use only the rear brake.
Use the front brake first, then the rear brake.
Use both brakes at the same time.

questions.correctAnswerText: Use both brakes at the same time.
questions.explanation: To stop quickly, apply both brakes at the same time.

questions.question: How can you be more visible at an intersection?

options.text: Make eye contact with other drivers.
Always use your headlight when riding.
Wave your arms.
Ride very close to the vehicle in front of you.

questions.correctAnswerText: Always use your headlight when riding.
questions.explanation: To be most visible at an intersection, ride with your headlight on. Position your motorcycle so oncoming traffic can see you clearly. Keep a safe distance from other vehicles so you have room to avoid danger. Do not rely on eye contact alone—drivers may not notice you.

questions.question: Which item is NOT protective clothing for a motorcycle rider?

options.text: Jacket
Boots
Gloves
Sandals

questions.correctAnswerText: Sandals
questions.explanation: Wear a helmet, eye protection, a jacket, long pants, sturdy boots, and gloves when riding. Sandals do not protect your feet.

questions.question: When should you flash your brake light?

options.text: When you are tired while riding.
When you will slow down where drivers do not expect it.
When there is a stop sign ahead.
When your signals are not working.

questions.correctAnswerText: When you will slow down where drivers do not expect it.
questions.explanation: Motorcycle brake lights are hard to see. Flash your brake light before slowing down in unexpected places, like the middle of a block or near an alley. This helps other drivers notice you are slowing.

questions.question: How can you tell if your rear tire has gone flat while riding?

options.text: You hear a hissing noise from the rear of the bike.
The back end jerks from side to side.
You cannot accelerate.
The rear brake does not work.

questions.correctAnswerText: The back end jerks from side to side.
questions.explanation: If your rear tire fails, the back of your motorcycle will jerk from side to side. You will rarely hear a tire fail while riding.

questions.question: If a tire goes flat while you are riding, what should you do?

options.text: Use both brakes and stop quickly.
Shift your weight toward the good tire.
Brake on the good tire and steer to the side of the road.
Relax your grip on the handlebars.

questions.correctAnswerText: Brake on the good tire and steer to the side of the road.
questions.explanation: Hold the handlebars firmly and ease off the throttle. Keep the motorcycle straight. Slowly apply the brake to the tire that is not flat. As you slow down, move to the side of the road, squeeze the clutch, and stop.

questions.question: When passing another vehicle, what should you do?

options.text: You may ride on the shoulder.
You may complete the pass in a no passing zone.
You must start and finish the pass in a passing zone.
You should sound your horn to make the driver slow down.

questions.correctAnswerText: You must start and finish the pass in a passing zone.
questions.explanation: All passing must happen in areas where it is safe and legal. Always follow speed limits while passing.

questions.question: If a tire goes flat and you must brake, what should you do?

options.text: Apply the brake of the tire that is not flat.
Apply the brake of the tire that is flat.
Apply both brakes.
Do not use either brake.

questions.correctAnswerText: Apply the brake of the tire that is not flat.
questions.explanation: If a tire goes flat and you must brake, slowly apply the brake of the tire that is still good.

questions.question: To make a quick stop on wet pavement, what should you do?

options.text: Use only the front brake.
Use only the rear brake.
Use both brakes.

questions.correctAnswerText: Use both brakes.
questions.explanation: Use both brakes for a quick stop on wet pavement. You can use the front brake on slippery surfaces if you apply it slowly to prevent it from locking.

questions.question: What reduces the risk of head or neck injury in a crash?

options.text: Riding on the shoulder
Riding under the speed limit
Wearing a helmet
Not allowing a passenger on the motorcycle

questions.correctAnswerText: Wearing a helmet
questions.explanation: Wearing a helmet is the best way to reduce head and neck injuries if you crash.

questions.question: How should you control your motorcycle while turning?

options.text: Speed up before entering the turn.
Keep the motorcycle from leaning.
Look through the turn to see what is ahead.
Come to a complete stop before entering the turn.

questions.correctAnswerText: Look through the turn to see what is ahead.
questions.explanation: To stay in control during a turn, look through the turn by turning your head only. Slow down before the turn and lean your motorcycle in the right direction.
